summary: This is a pre-commit configuration file that sets up automated checks to run before code is committed to a repository. It excludes certain directories from checking, then defines multiple tools that validate file quality — checking for large files, YAML syntax, markdown formatting, broken links, and spelling errors — to catch common issues before they're committed.

explanations.2: This pattern tells pre-commit to skip checking files in these three directories: the build output folder, the git metadata folder, and the quarto cache folder.
explanations.7: This specifies which version of the pre-commit-hooks repository to use — think of it like pinning a dependency so you get consistent behavior across machines.
explanations.24: This tells the markdown linter where to find its configuration file, so it knows which style rules to enforce.
explanations.33: This declares that the markdown-link-check tool is written in Node.js, so pre-commit knows it needs to use Node to run it.
explanations.45: This bash command extracts just the YAML header (everything between the first pair of --- lines) from a Quarto file, then validates it with yq; it's checking that the metadata at the top of each file is properly formatted.
explanations.48: The {} placeholder gets replaced with the actual filename being checked, so each Quarto file gets validated one at a time.
explanations.49: This restricts the hook to only run on files ending in .qmd (Quarto markdown files), not on every file in the repo.
explanations.64: This tells cspell to skip checking anything inside _extensions folders, which contain third-party code that shouldn't be spell-checked.
